issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a StockIngredient constructor with three parameters StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template repository's StockIngredient class only provides a four-parameter constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean). The solution repository uses the three-parameter constructor. This mismatch will confuse students and prevent them from instantiating StockIngredient as described in the assignment and shown in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a three-argument constructor public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) in the template's StockIngredient class (or overload the existing constructor) that performs the same validation/assignments as in the solution. This aligns the template with the UML/problem statement and the reference solution, allowing students to instantiate StockIngredient as expected.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a StockIngredient constructor with signature StockIngredient(String, int, int), but the template repository provides only a four-argument constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int, boolean). This mismatch in the constructor API (same conceptual entity but different parameterization) will confuse students and likely cause compilation errors when they follow the problem description and solution examples that instantiate StockIngredient with three arguments.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a three-argument constructor in the template StockIngredient class to match the problem statement and solution API. For example, add: public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) { this(name, price, quantity, false); } This preserves the existing strictValidation constructor while aligning the public API with the exercise description and solution.
